newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SmarTone expected to attract long-term interest.
newsitem.headline: SmarTone expected to attract long-term interest.

text.p: The prospect of steady growth at SmarTone Mobile Communications Ltd is attracting interest from long-term investors but retail investors appear to find the Hong Kong mobile communicator's IPO too pricey.
Market sources described as mixed the response from local investors to SmarTone's 84 million share global initial public offering, which closes on Friday.
International interest was more encouraging, they said on Wednesday.
A total of 12.6 million shares are being offered in Hong Kong at HK$21.25 (US$2.91) a share, subject to adjustment. Trading on the Hong Kong stock market is expected to start on October 30.
Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage, said longer-term investors, particularly overseas funds, had the financial muscle to wait for returns.
"But it is not the case for local short-term speculators," he said.
"Overseas investors are interested in accumulating this kind of high-tech stock for a long-term investment because they normally have a better anticipation of the industry earnings," Au said.
SmarTone posted a turnover of HK$1.62 billion in fiscal 1996, up from HK$988 million in fiscal 1995 and HK$474 million in 1994.
In its listing prospectus, the company forecast fiscal 1997 net profit of not less than HK$610 million, an increase of 61 percent over fiscal 1996.

Michael Ng, an analyst for ASG Investment, said the issue was considered expensive, with a current price range of HK$17.25 to HK$21.25 per share, giving a fully diluted price earnings multiple of 13.1 to 16.10 times 1997 earnings.
Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd trades at a multiple of about 15 times, he said.
Analysts said investors may also be concerned about the firm's prospects in the face of keen competition in the Hong Kong mobile phone market.
SmarTone was an unsuccessful bidder for one of six 10-year Personal Communications Services (PCS) licences awarded by the Hong Kong government in September.

Analysts said the introduction of PCS would heighten competition in Hong Kong's cellular communications market and lead to an overall reduction in prices, but added SmarTone and its three rivals had a headstart on the competition.

"We are concerned about its long-term prospects," said Kelvin Tang, investment analyst with Impac Asset Management (HK) Ltd. "Its short-term (prospects) are OK due to its established position and strong profit track record."

SmarTone said in its listing prospectus that it planned to spend HK$2.1 billion over the next four years to expand its network capacity to 600,000 subscribers from about 259,000 and improve its coverage.
It also said it was focusing on telecommunications opportunities in China.
Analysts said the company's potential for penetrating the mainland telecommunications industry underpinned the interest shown by overseas investors keen to tap the growing China market.

The company is 40 percent owned by Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, 30 percent by AT&T Wireless Communications, 15 percent by ABC Communications (Holdings) Ltd, and 15 percent by Town Khan Ltd, a unit of China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications.
